passage: At the lift of their Mumbai building, two-year-old Ramesh waved hard at the watchman. "Bye-bye!" he shouted, and the watchman waved back. Upstairs, a neighbour came to the door, beaming, and said, "Hello, Ramesh!" Ramesh pressed his face into his father's leg. Jatin did not push him. "He'll say hello when he's ready," he told her. Later Ramesh peeked out and gave a tiny wave.

qa.q: Who did Ramesh wave to at the lift?
qa.a: He waved at the watchman.

qa.q: Why did Ramesh hide his face when the neighbour said hello, and what else could it mean?
qa.a: He was probably feeling shy about a person he does not know well. It could also be that he was tired after the outing.

qa.q: What did Jatin do well, and what might he try next?
qa.a: He did not force a greeting, so Ramesh stayed comfortable. He could let Ramesh watch the neighbour chat for a while before a wave. 🙂

qa.q: How might the neighbour feel about being greeted by hiding?
qa.a: She might feel a little disappointed at first, but Jatin's explanation and the later tiny wave can help her see it as shyness.

grounding: A toddler waves and says bye-bye to show social interest, but shyness may lead to hiding and adults do not force a greeting.

passage:
"Arohi, look, Nikhil Uncle is here. Say hello!"
"No." Arohi ducked behind the curtain.
"That's okay," said Hansa. "Hello can wait."
"Hello, Arohi," said the visitor, smiling. "I like your curtain fort."
A pause. A small eye peeked out.
"Bye-bye," she said an hour later at the door, and waved.
"Bye, Arohi!" said the visitor.
Hansa grinned.

qa.q: Where did Arohi hide when the visitor arrived?
qa.a: She hid behind the curtain.

qa.q: What was Arohi probably feeling while she hid, and what else could explain it?
qa.a: She was probably feeling shy with a person she does not know well. She might also have been in the middle of a game and not wanted to stop.

qa.q: What did Hansa and the visitor do that helped?
qa.a: Hansa did not push for a hello, and the visitor spoke gently about her fort. Arohi could warm up in her own time.

qa.q: What would change if Hansa had insisted on a hello?
qa.a: Arohi might have hidden more, or cried, and the visitor might feel awkward too.

grounding: A shy toddler may hide instead of greeting, and adults do not force a greeting; later she waves goodbye.

passage: Daycare note, Tuesday. At pick-up time Himani waves "bah-bah!" to everyone, the cook, the guard, the other parents. But today, when the visiting inspector bent down and said hello, she hid behind my legs and wouldn't look. Her mother said, "Say hello, Himani!" I suggested we let her be. When the inspector was leaving, Himani peeked out and waved a tiny wave. Salma, daycare teacher

qa.q: Whom does Himani usually wave to at pick-up?
qa.a: The cook, the guard and the other parents.

qa.q: What was Himani feeling when she hid from the inspector?
qa.a: She was shy with a new person; her tiny wave later shows she was still interested once she had time.

qa.q: Which choice of Salma's worked, and why?
qa.a: Suggesting they let her be worked, because without pressure Himani found her own moment to wave.

qa.q: How does Himani's mother see the hiding?
qa.a: She seems to want Himani to be polite, perhaps feeling a little embarrassed in front of the inspector.

grounding: A teacher sees a toddler wave to familiar people and hide from a new one, and does not force a greeting.

passage:
At the small-town bus stand, Aadhya waved her whole arm at the conductor hanging out of the bus door. "Hai! Hai!" He waved back, and she squealed.
Then the temple priest stopped and bent down. "And hello to you, little one!" Aadhya pressed her face into her Bua's sari.
"Say namaste," someone said.
Himani, her Bua, shook her head. "She'll say it another day." The priest smiled and walked on.

qa.q: Who was hanging out of the bus door?
qa.a: The conductor.

qa.q: What was Aadhya feeling when she pressed her face into her Bua's sari?
qa.a: She felt shy with the priest bending close, even though she had been happily waving at the conductor from a distance.

qa.q: Which of Himani's choices respected Aadhya, and why?
qa.a: Not forcing her to say namaste respected her shyness and let her greet when she felt ready.

qa.q: How might the priest see Aadhya hiding?
qa.a: The priest seems understanding, smiling and walking on without taking offence.

grounding: A toddler waves and babbles hello to a familiar face but hides from a stranger, and her aunt doesn't force a greeting.

passage:
Every morning in Sapporo, Hiroshi stood at the window and waved "bai-bai!" to the garbage truck crew. They always waved back.
On Saturday, a new neighbour at the gate smiled and said, "Good morning, Hiroshi!" He ducked behind Hana's coat.
Hana didn't pull him forward. She smiled at the neighbour. "He's shy with new faces." From behind the coat, Hiroshi peeped out and watched.

qa.q: Whom does Hiroshi wave to every morning?
qa.a: The garbage truck crew.

qa.q: What was Hiroshi feeling when he ducked behind Hana's coat?
qa.a: He felt shy and unsure with a new face, even though he's friendly with people he knows.

qa.q: What did Hana do that respected Hiroshi?
qa.a: She didn't pull him forward, and explained his shyness kindly to the neighbour.

qa.q: How might the new neighbour feel when Hiroshi hides?
qa.a: The neighbour might feel a little disappointed, but Hana's words help them understand it isn't personal.

grounding: A toddler waves to familiar faces and hides from a new neighbour, and his mother doesn't force a greeting.

passage:
I'm Kunal, from upstairs. Most mornings little Madhuri waves bye-bye to the milkman, and when she sees me on the stairs she babbles, “Aa-lo!” and flaps her hand.
Last Sunday my friend came with me. Madhuri took one look at him and hid behind her mother's dupatta.
“Say hello, Madhuri,” my friend said.
Her mother just smiled. “She's shy today. No need.” Madhuri peeped out at me and gave a tiny wave.

qa.q: Who does Madhuri wave bye-bye to most mornings?
qa.a: She waves bye-bye to the milkman.

qa.q: What was Madhuri feeling when she hid behind her mother's dupatta?
qa.a: She was shy and unsure of the new person, while still feeling friendly towards Kunal, whom she knew.

qa.q: Why was her mother right not to force a hello?
qa.a: Forcing a greeting on a shy toddler can add to her unease; letting her choose meant she still gave a tiny wave.

qa.q: How might Kunal's friend have felt when Madhuri hid?
qa.a: The friend may have felt a little disappointed or awkward, expecting a hello.

grounding: It shows a toddler waving and babbling hello to people she knows and hiding when shy, with an adult not forcing a greeting.
